rules.rule:
Focus on correctness, regression risk, error handling, interface consistency, and missing tests. Distinguish concrete defects from optional improvements.

Apply code-minimality review. Flag when the diff reimplements an existing helper, module, or installed dependency that could be reused; introduces an unnecessary abstraction such as a wrapper, adapter, factory, registry, manager, or service layer; adds a third-party dependency where the standard library or a platform-native capability already suffices; could shrink its change scope; could delete code instead of extending it; or adds YAGNI-style speculative capability. For bug fixes, flag symptom patches (workaround, special case, extra fallback) that leave the root cause unrepaired. Tag these findings with an internal category: delete, reuse, stdlib, native, yagni, shrink, or root-cause. Keep the existing review output format. Code minimality is advisory only: never recommend removing or weakening input validation, error handling, permission or security checks, auditability, accessibility, or deterministic gate behavior, and never accept fewer lines as a reason to cut them.
